title: Comprehensive analysis of liver macrophage composition by flow cytometry and immunofluorescence in murine NASH
protocol: Cover the surface of a plastic tray with a sheet of absorbent bench paper.
Layer two paper towels over the bench paper.

Assemble surgical tools including scissor, tweezer, suture, catheter, cotton tips, razor blade, petri dishes, paper towels, pump, tubing for the pump, PBS bottle, beaker, 70% ethanol, and biohazard bags.
Attach the inlet end of the tubing to the peristaltic pump and place it into the PBS bottle.
Place the outlet end of the tubing into a beaker.
Start the pump until air is cleared from the line and the tubing is filled with PBS.
Set up reagents for harvest.
Prepare complete DMEM and FACS buffer.
Prepare and label 3 sets of 50 mL conical tubes for each liver sample.
Prepare digestion buffer in the first set of 50 ml conical tubes.
Perfuse mouse liver.
Euthanize the mouse using carbon dioxide and subsequently perform cervical dislocation.
Weigh and record the body weight of the mouse using a balance.
Place the mouse in a prone position.
Sterilize the abdomen with 70% ethanol.
Use a tweezer to lift up the skin near the genitals and make an incision with scissors.
Pull the skin up to expose the body cavity membrane.
Carefully cut open the peritoneal cavity membrane and move the small intestines aside to fully expose the liver.
Locate the portal vein underneath the liver.
Place a suture underneath the vein and secure a half-knot.
Cannulate the portal vein with the catheter until its tip reaches the branching point of the vein and passes the half-knotted suture.
Tighten the knot to secure the catheter and remove the needle.
Cut the inferior vena cava below the liver to release blood and PBS from the liver immediately after attaching the tubing onto the catheter.
Perfuse the portal vein with PBS using the peristaltic pump at a rate of 5 mL/min prior to inserting the tubing onto the catheter to prevent air bubbles.
Increase the flow rate to 10 mL/min.
Apply gentle pressure on the IVC periodically.
Massage the liver with a cotton-tipped wood applicator to promote clearance of sinusoidal blood.
Perfuse for a minimum of 3 min or until the liver is completely pale.
Remove the catheter from the liver.
Suture and gallbladder removal should also be performed.
Resect the liver from the body cavity.
Weigh and record the total liver weight.
Resect specific lobes of the liver for downstream analyses: left medial and lateral lobe for flow cytometry, right lateral lobe for immunofluorescence.
For flow cytometry, use between 0.5-1 gm of tissue.
Submerge tissue into 500–750 μL formalin and incubate at 4°C for 24 h for histology processing.
Transfer the tissue into 70% ethanol for subsequent paraffin embedding after formalin treatment.
Flash freeze tissue in liquid nitrogen for RNA, protein, or triglyceride quantification.
Weigh and record the liver tissue dedicated for flow cytometry.
Place the liver in a petri dish and mince finely with a razor blade.
Transfer the minced liver into a prepared digestion buffer and keep on ice until the end of the tissue harvest.
Warm up all samples in a 37°C water bath for 5 min at the end of the harvest.
Place the liver mixture on a shaker at 37°C with rotation for 30 min to digest.
Vortex mixture after 15 min.
Pre-wet 70 μm cell strainers placed onto new 50 mL falcon tubes with 5 mL cold complete DMEM.
Transfer the digested liver mixture onto the cell strainers to allow pass-through of cells into the new 50 mL tubes.
Add 15 mL cold complete DMEM to the original tubes.
Pour the rinse onto the cell strainers while mashing undigested liver pieces using a syringe plunger end.
Centrifuge the strained cell suspension at 50 × g for 3 minutes at 4°C.
Carefully pour the supernatant containing NPCs into a new 50 mL falcon tube.
Discard the pellet containing hepatocytes.
Centrifuge the NPC suspension at 163 g for 7 minutes at 4°C to pellet the NPCs.
Discard the supernatant.
Resuspend the NPC pellet with 1 mL ACK lysis buffer and incubate for 5 minutes, at 20°C to lyse red blood cells.
Add 10 mL PBS to wash the cells.
Centrifuge the cell suspension at 163 g for 7 minutes at 4°C to re-pellet the NPCs.
Resuspend the cells in 1 mL PBS and transfer to 1.5 mL Eppendorf tubes.
Keep the samples on ice until ready to proceed to the next step.
Pellet the cells using a bench-top centrifuge at 650 × g for 3.5 min at 4°C.
Wash and exchange buffer containing BSA with PBS if present.
Resuspend pellet in 100 μL Zombie Aqua solution at 1:250 dilution in PBS for live/dead stain.
Incubate on ice and in the dark for 15 min.
Wash the cells by adding 700 μL of FACS buffer to cell suspension.
Pellet the cells at 650 × g for 3.5 min at 4°C.
Aspirate the supernatant.
Resuspend the pellet with 10 μL Fc block solution.
Incubate on ice and in the dark for 5 min.
Add 90 μL of antibody cocktail to the cell suspension.
Resuspend and incubate on ice and in the dark for at least 45 min.
Wash the cells by adding 700 μL FACS buffer to the cell suspension.
Pellet the cells at 650 × g for 3.5 min at 4°C.
Aspirate the supernatant.
Resuspend the cells in 300 μL FACS buffer.
Filter the cell suspension through a 70-μm cell strainer into 5 mL polystyrene round-bottom flow tube.
Keep on ice in the dark.
The samples are now ready to be analyzed on a flow cytometer.
Harvest liver lobe and place the tissue into a tube containing formalin.
Ensure the tissue is submerged in formalin, typically requiring a volume of 500–700 μL of fixative.
Incubate at 4°C for 24 h.
Transfer liver lobe to 750 μL 30% sucrose in PBS at 4°C for 24 h.
Submerge and freeze liver lobe in OCT in mold and store at -80°C.
Cut 8 μM tissue sections using a cryostat on glass slides.
Store frozen slides at −80°C.
Prepare 50 mL blocking buffer fresh on the day of staining.
Retrieve frozen slides from −80°C and let them air dry for 15–20 min at 20°C.
Incubate slides in PBS for 5 min in a glass chamber.
Incubate slides in blocking buffer for 45 min.
Prepare primary antibody, 50 μL per section, in blocking buffer.
Extract slides from the glass chamber and dry around the tissue sections with Kimwipe.
Encircle sections using a hydrophobic pen.
Add 50 μL primary antibody solution on each section.
Incubate slides in a container on wet paper towels for 16–24 h at 4°C.
Incubate slides in PBS for 5 min in the glass chamber, wash three times.
Dry slides around the tissue sections with Kimwipe after washing.
Re-apply hydrophobic barrier using pen if necessary.
Prepare secondary antibody solution and add 50 μL per section.
Incubate for 1 h at room temperature in the dark.
Incubate slides in PBS for 5 min in a glass chamber, wash two times.
Prepare 50 mL Hoechst dye (1:25000).
Add Hoechst dye solution to slides in the glass chamber.
Retrieve slides from the glass chamber.
Dry the slides carefully.
Apply a small drop of prolong gold antifade reagent on each slide.
Place a cover slip on top of each slide.
Let the slides dry for at least 1 hour in the dark.
Image the slides with light or confocal microscopy within one week of staining.
